item.text: I’ll read the service documentation first, then build a retrying reconciliation pass that deduplicates before filtering and validates the final JSON invariants.

item.aggregated_output:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: OrderService/1.0 Python/3.11.2
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 15:36:43 GMT
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 1015

item.text: The docs confirm 50-item pagination plus short-lived bearer tokens. I’m now traversing every page with token refresh and rate-limit retries, counting repeated IDs globally before applying the exact UTC/status rules, and caching customer lookups.

The full pass completed: 30 pages, 1,480 distinct order IDs, and 20 repeated listings discarded. The qualifying set contains 407 exactly-`shipped` orders; I’m writing the result and running final schema/arithmetic checks now.

import json
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('/workspace/result.json')
assert p.exists()
r=json.loads(p.read_text())
assert list(r)==['total_cents','order_count','duplicates_skipped','by_region']
assert list(r['by_region'])==['north','south','east','west']
assert all(type(v) is int for k,v in r.items() if k"'!='"'by_region')
assert all(type(v) is int for v in r['by_region'].values())
assert sum(r['by_region'].values())==r['total_cents']
print(json.dumps(r, separators=(',',':')))
print('VALID')
PY"
